Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:00 UTC (scheduled 45m, actual 52m)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood - intro), Anika Rao (CTO - HarborTech), Marcus Li (DevOps), Tom Bower (Security Manager), Lena Ortiz (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
HarborTech is evaluating Redwood private deployment for LLM inference. Primary concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress IPs and regional restrictions for EU customers, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 evidence, and a performance benchmark. Discussed options: private control plane with private endpoints, transit gateway peering, Direct Connect for onprem, and dedicated capacity pilot. Next steps include sharing network template and SOC docs, scheduling a deeper network workshop, and provisioning a short pilot.

Topics noticed: Networking topology, egress IP management, region gating, private endpoints, KMS, audit logs

Action items (captured): Jordan will send docs; Priya to prepare benchmarks; Marcus to send VPC details; Tom to list compliance regions.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya our SE.
[00:08] Anika: Hi Jordan, thanks. I'm Anika Rao, CTO at HarborTech. Marcus, Tom, Lena are here with me. Quick note, we're short on time so if we can focus on the networking pieces that'd be great.
[00:18] Jordan: Absolutely. Priya, want to kick off on the high-level private deployment options?
[00:22] Priya: Yeah, sure. So Redwood's private offering gives you two flavors practically — a private control plane with managed connectors and private endpoints, or a fully on-prem style package. For most customers with cloud VPCs we do VPC peering, Privatelink-style endpoints, or Transit Gateway peering depending on scale and cross-region needs.
[00:40] Marcus: Right, we — sorry — we run in AWS primarily, we have a Transit Gateway in us-east-1 and some peering in eu-west-1 for EU workloads. Our ask is we need egress IP stability — some customers whitelist IPs. How do you handle fixed egress IPs from Redwood private?
[00:56] Priya: Good Q. For Hosted we have dynamic pool IPs, but for Private we can route through our managed NAT or you can terminate egress through your own NAT/Direct Connect. Practically we support two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed egress with a small set of stable IPs per region (requires contract and dedicated capacity), or 2) hairpin/egress back through customer's Transit Gateway or Direct Connect so egress appears from your network. Option 2 is preferred for strict allowlist policies.
[01:25] Tom: When you say "stable IPs per region" — is that a single IP or a block? Our security team wants an IP block we can whitelist.
[01:31] Priya: It can be an IP block — typically a /29 or /28 depending on throughput and HA. If you go Redwood-managed egress we allocate a small range and publish those. If you route egress through your TGW, then it's whatever your egress uses.
[01:45] Lena: If we route back through our TGW, is there an additional latency hit? We have tight SLOs — inference p99 under 200ms for short prompts.
[01:53] Priya: There's a tradeoff. Hairpinning to your TGW adds a few dozen milliseconds usually — depends on region hops. For p99 under 200ms it's doable if the model is in the same region and we avoid cross-region hops. For stricter latency you might prefer dedicated capacity in-region and Redwood-managed egress with direct peering.
[02:13] Anika: We're evaluating both Dedicated and Private. The Dedicated reserved pools looked attractive for throughput but we need the private network footprint as well. Can Dedicated be combined with Private VPC peering?
[02:24] Jordan: Yes — Dedicated refers to reserved GPU pools and Dedicated capacity can be deployed into a private VPC environment. So you can have reserved throughput with private networking. We typically pair those for enterprise grade.
[02:34] Marcus: Ok. On the topic of peering, we have overlapping CIDRs in some accounts — is there support for NATing or IP remapping on Redwood side?
[02:43] Priya: We don't do IP remapping on our control plane, but when using Transit Gateway peering or a private gateway we can route via a managed NAT or use PrivateLink endpoints per account to avoid CIDR overlap. PrivateLink avoids peering and is usually better when CIDRs overlap.
[03:00] Tom: Regarding PrivateLink, does each service endpoint consume ENIs on our side? Any quota concerns?
[03:06] Priya: Yes, PrivateLink creates endpoint ENIs in your subnets. You'll want enough subnet capacity and ENI quota. We can provide guidance on subnet sizing; for high throughput we recommend dedicated subnets across AZs.
[03:15] Marcus: What's the recommended connection for on-prem? We have a colo and DX to AWS, would you prefer we hairpin via DX?
[03:22] Priya: Direct Connect + routing via TGW is a common pattern. You can keep data path entirely inside your network using TGW and DX, which satisfies egress and data residency needs.
[03:30] Jordan: Quick clarifying Q — are you planning to keep EU customer data in eu-west only, or do you have EU users that can be served from us-east?
[03:37] Anika: We need EU data to stay in EU regions — data residency requirement from our privacy team. So model inference for EU customers must not leave eu-west-1 or eu-west-2 without explicit controls.
[03:47] Priya: Understood. Redwood supports regional pinning: you can pin model versions and route requests to EU region-only deployments. We'll need to configure per-route policies and can set fallbacks off so no cross-region fails.
[03:58] Tom: Audit and key management — KMS integration is required for us. Do you support customer-managed keys? HSM?
[04:06] Priya: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. HSM-backed keys are possible through our KMS connectors depending on provider. For Hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS but for Private you bring your KMS. Logs and audit trails can integrate with your SIEM.
[04:20] Marcus: A bunch of our infra is automated via Terraform. How does onboarding look — do you give CloudFormation/Terraform modules?
[04:27] Jordan: We provide Terraform modules and a network diagram template. Priya will share the private deployment checklist repo; it's not public but we'll send you a sanitized template.
[04:35] Anika: Cool. On compliance, we need SOC 2 type II evidence and change logs/audit logs. Do you have SOC2 and can you surface audit logs per-tenant?
[04:44] Priya: Redwood is SOC2 compliant — we can share the SOC2 report under NDA. For Private you get audit logs in your logging pipeline; we can forward request-level logs to your account, with PII redaction options.
[04:56] Marcus: I want to call out a specific networking constraint — our EU VPC uses strict route tables and doesn't allow transitive routing from vendor accounts. So we can't accept peering that causes transitive access; only PrivateLink or direct TGW attachments from our account. Thoughts?
[05:12] Priya: PrivateLink or TGW attachments where Redwood's infra sits in a partner account and you attach via TGW are both feasible; we just need to map out the route tables and avoid transitive routes. We'll propose a TGW attachment pattern that keeps routes explicit.
[05:27] Tom: Any special things around egress for GDPR requests if data must be deleted — can you guarantee no downstream backups exist in another region?
[05:35] Priya: For Private deployments, data residency controlled — we can avoid replicating logs cross-region. Deletion requests can be configured to remove user data; we'll need to scope retention windows and work with your legal team on SLAs for deletion.
[05:48] Anika: Great. For performance, we plan to exercise a couple of models: a mid-sized Llama-like open model for chat and a text-embedding workflow. We need guidance on quantization and expected throughput.
[06:00] Priya: We'll run a benchmark during pilot. For embeddings, you typically see higher token throughput — we recommend a quantized model for inference cost savings. I'll prepare quantization recommendations and expected throughput/latency baselines for the models you listed.
[06:13] Jordan: Quick procurement note — some enterprises require vendor subnet ACLs and proof of egress ranges in the SOW to whitelist. We can include that in the pilot SOW.
[06:22] Marcus: That'd help. Also can you provide a list of ports/protocols required for the private endpoints?
[06:28] Priya: We'll include a network appendix — ports (443 TLS for API), optional metrics/monitoring ports if you want SNMP/agenting, and the PrivateLink ENI traffic.
[06:38] Marcus: Is there support for mutual TLS between our services and Redwood endpoint? We prefer mTLS for service-to-service auth.
[06:44] Priya: Most traffic is over TLS with token-based auth, but mTLS is possible in PrivateLink setups — it's something we can add onto the private endpoint. We'll note that as an implementation option.
[06:53] Anika: Another constraint — some EU customers require physical separation (no shared GPU across tenants). Can you guarantee dedicated GPUs for certain tenants?
[07:01] Priya: Yes, that's what Dedicated reserved pools are for — you can have dedicated GPU capacity that we don't multi-tenant. That can be combined with Private networking and regional pinning.
[07:10] Tom: About logging — does Redwood redact sensitive fields in logs by default? We need PII redaction before logs leave our VPC.
[07:18] Priya: For Private flows, request logs can be retained in your account; we can apply a redaction pipeline before forwarding anything to us. We can also support on-host redaction plug-ins.
[07:28] Jordan: We'll pause on architecture for a sec. Marcus, can you confirm the people we should include in the network deep-dive?
[07:34] Marcus: It'll be me, our network infra engineer (Lena is here), and our colo lead — I'll invite them. Also Tom for the compliance bits.
[07:42] Jordan: Great. Priya, can you outline what you'll share post-call?
[07:45] Priya: I'll share: private deployment checklist, Terraform modules, network diagram template, list of egress IP ranges for managed option, SOC2 docs (NDA), and a rough draft SOW for a 2-week dedicated pilot.
[07:58] Samir: Quick note — we'll include a sample cost sheet for dedicated capacity vs hosted usage so you can do unit economics.
[08:04] Anika: That would be useful. On procurement timeline — we aim to have a pilot lined up in December if legal is ok. Any red flags on procurement side?
[08:14] Jordan: Standard enterprise procurement review. We can support a one-off pilot agreement and then expand to a reserved capacity contract.
[08:20] Tom: One small thing — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for team management for the console in Private?
[08:27] Priya: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for Private, with RBAC mapping to your IdP.
[08:33] Marcus: For the pilot, what telemetry will you need from our side to run benchmarks? We'll need to know exact endpoints, sample payloads etc.
[08:41] Priya: We'll send a benchmark template (requests per second, payload sizes, concurrency). For embeddings we'll ask for sample corpus sizes. We'll instrument both sides to capture p50/p90/p99 and token costs.
[08:52] Anika: Does Redwood support encryption of KV cache? We have concerns that cached prefixes could surface PII.
[08:59] Priya: The KV cache can be encrypted at rest and optional customer KMS can be used. We also support configurable cache policies to avoid caching sensitive inputs.
[09:09] Tom: Perfect. Any notes on fallbacks if regional capacity is constrained — can you automatically fail over to another compatible model in-region or -- I guess that's cross-region.
[09:19] Priya: We support policy-driven fallbacks. For strict residency you can disable cross-region fallback. Otherwise we can fallback to a quantized or smaller variant in same region to keep availability.
[09:30] Jordan: Ok sounds like good alignment. Quick recap for next steps: we'll share docs, schedule deep-dive, and propose pilot SOW. Anyone want to add or correct?
[09:40] Anika: Sounds right. One thing — please include an explicit line about egress IP block size in the SOW so my team can pre-approve.
[09:47] Jordan: Noted. Priya, anything else?
[09:50] Priya: I'll include port list, mTLS notes, and subnet sizing suggestions. Also a note about PrivateLink ENI quotas.
[09:59] Marcus: Ok that helps. Tom, anything on compliance front?
[10:02] Tom: Just the SOC2 and a deletion SLA — if you can give a candidate SLA for deletion, that'd be great.
[10:08] Priya: We'll propose a 30-day max for deletion in the pilot SOW, subject to legal review.
[10:13] Anika: Great. Let's set the follow-up — Marcus and Priya will do the network deep-dive week of 11/23, Jordan will send docs by tomorrow.
[10:22] Jordan: Yep. I'll send the bundle by 11/18. Big thanks everyone, we'll follow up on calendar invites.
[10:28] Samir: Thanks all.
[10:30] Anika: Thanks, bye.
